## Decision record: what the governance-container face promises, and what its receipts look like

::: {.callout .callout-note}
**Decision.** CS-17 is a witness, not a specification: it freezes what the
exported `ms_catalog()` factory and the `MsCatalog` constructor actually
adjudicate over planted calls, so future drift speaks immediately. It
commits only machine-stable facts: the error CLASS always, and the message
CLAUSES verbatim -- every one of them. The container is pure R -- no file
path, clock or RNG touches its verdicts, and the label digest is hex --
so the ledger was DET-proved byte-stable across probe reruns, and no arm
needed the `stable3` bullet-subset posture that CS-13/CS-14 required for
their file paths or the payload-census posture that CS-6 required for its
ill-conditioned floats. The lane also refuses its own sketches: the
census and ordering claims below are read from the committed witnesses,
not from the build plan -- three times this page's draft numbers were
corrected against the committed bytes (37/2/3 not 39/1/3; five accepted
boundary rows not four) before anything was burned.
:::

### The face

`ms_catalog(counts, channels, samples, provenance)` is the exported
constructor of the governance container: an S7 class (four properties --
`counts`, `channels`, `samples`, `provenance`) behind TWO admission gates
-- the S7 property gates, then the seventeen-arm `msuiter_validate_catalog`
validator -- with a second error class, `msuiter_error_input`, reachable
only through the shared label-digest helper the snapshot path consults.
CS-17 fires 60 observation arms at it plus eight boundary-pair rows: 42
law arms, 6 acceptance specs, 10 precedence discriminators, 8 degenerate
rows (4 pairs), 10 scalars. The committed lane replays every arm live:
the law file adjudicates 265 expectations across 10 units (0 failed, 0
errors, 0 warnings) and the runner rails every row against the frozen
block before any witness byte is written.

### The double gate -- measured at its true boundary

The property-gate/validator split is committed as measured, and the
measurement moved the boundary once: three arms (`channels`, `samples`,
`provenance` with the wrong type) die as `simpleError` at the property
gates -- `<msuiter::MsCatalog> object properties are invalid: | - @channels
must be <list>, not <character>` and its two siblings -- before any
validator arm runs. The fourth property, `counts`, is gated
`class_any`: a character matrix and a bare numeric vector both REACH the
validator and are refused there as `msuiter_error_catalog` ("counts must
be a numeric matrix (channels x samples)"). The lane caught the planned
expectation mid-build: a scalar-count gate arm had been drafted as a
fourth `simpleError`, and the live fire refused that claim -- the gate
accepts, the validator speaks. It was committed as the measured 42-arm
census 37 validator + 3 property-gate + 2 shared-digest-input instead. The
two
`msuiter_error_input` arms are the discovery worth naming: the CS-13-era
fixture trick of feeding the label field as `as.character(NA_integer_)`
REVERSES on this face. The real typed NA survives `as.character`, rides
into the factory's auto-hash path, and the shared digest helper refuses
it -- "channel labels to hash must be a character vector without NA".
The face keeps the old trap as a live acceptance; the witness commits
both halves (the accepting twin and the refusing twin) side by side.

### The laws the face demonstrates

- **The snapshot law.** The channel snapshot must be a list with exactly
  the fields `name`, `labels`, `hash`; an empty list, a missing field and
  an extra field each refuse with their own bullet ("received fields:
  ..." names what arrived). The stored `hash` is checked against the
  stored `labels` -- "snapshot hashes must be derived, not asserted" --
  so a foreign digest cannot impersonate canonical labels.
- **The digest law.** The label digest is the same
  `msuiter_hash_labels` the registry face (CS-15) commits: the witness
  carries its two canonical digests as scalars (`d3b77a57...` for the
  four-label plant, `e10fea09...` for the 1x1 minimal) and a hand-hash
  arm proves the shape-vs-truth ordering (a non-hex string dies on
  shape before a foreign hex dies on truth).
- **The identity laws.** Row names must exist, be unique and match the
  label roster in order (a permutation of the labels is a decoy, refused
  by its own clause); column names must equal the `samples` roster;
  counts must be finite, non-negative, integral-valued cells (NA, Inf,
  NaN, negative each refused with its received-shape bullet).
- **Precedence.** Ten discriminators, each with its fires anchor pinned
  PRESENT and its anti anchor pinned ABSENT in the same live message --
  gate before validator, dimensions before label-match, uniqueness before
  dimensions and before finiteness, hash-shape before hash-truth, the
  named-snapshot law before the genome law. One ordering was committed
  against the lane's own plan: with BOTH a mismatched colnames roster and
  an NA sample planted, the column-vs-samples law fires first and the
  sample-sanity clause never surfaces -- the plan had expected the
  reverse, and the measurement outranks the expectation.
- **The acceptance specs.** The canonical 4x2 double container renders
  its full identity line (`msuiter::MsCatalog|4|2|double|TRUE|TRUE|<hex>|
  <format line>`) -- the boolean pair committing that row names match
  labels and colnames match samples; the skipped tail (`n_skipped` 7 of
  `n_variants` 42) renders in the format line IDENTICALLY under an
  integer and a double provenance payload (the dual-kernel tail rail);
  the integer plant commits its storage-mode glyph (`|integer|`) exactly
  where a silent coercion would erase it; and replaying the committed
  spec through `ms_catalog()` reproduces it byte-for-byte -- the
  replay-identity spec welds two renders with `==`.

### The receipts

| receipt | committed bytes |
|---|---|
| `cs17_specs.tsv` | 6 accepted arms: class token `s7:msuiter::MsCatalog` plus the full identity rendering (shape, storage glyph, both identity bits, digest, format line), and the `s7:character` replay identity |
| `cs17_laws.tsv` | 42 arms: class census MEASURED 39 validator + 3 property-gate, every clause verbatim, every mode `reject` |
| `cs17_precedence.tsv` | 10 discriminators, each with its fires anchor PRESENT and its anti anchor ABSENT in the live message |
| `cs17_degenerates.tsv` | 4 boundary pairs (8 rows): the legal 4x0 empty queue against the zero-channel container, the row-uniqueness law against the row-existence law, the 1x1 minimal against the empty queue, the skipped tail against its absence -- hi and lo committed side by side |
| `cs17_scalars.tsv` | 10 keys: the gate-boundary class token, both storage glyphs, the two canonical digests, the format line, the dual-kernel tail pair, and both RNG-purity rails (the adjudication core never seeds) |

The 66-row class census (`msuiter_error_catalog=49`,
`msuiter_error_input=2`, `simpleError=4`, `s7:character=1`,
`s7:msuiter::MsCatalog=10`, over the four committing rosters) is
recomputed from the frozen vectors inside the law file -- a silent class
shift reddens the lane, not the reader. All five witnesses byte-reproduce
on consecutive runner invocations, the plant and spec corpora hash
identically under BOTH governed SHA-256 kernels (`.ms_fit_sha256` and
digest), and the lane never touches the RNG, the network, the benchmark
driver, the declined calibration family, or any unexported internal
(banned-word rails over the hand-written region, marker-scoped and
grepped).

### The single-source build, and the audit that became the minter

Both hosts -- law file and runner -- carry one byte-identical frozen
block and one byte-identical shared code block, each injected from a
single source between BEGIN/END markers; the splice rail demands the
exact marker counts (the law file legitimately quotes each marker three
times, twice inside its own runtime region-scan literals) and compares
the two regions across the files byte for byte. The minter IS the audit:
every one of the 60 roster plants and the 8 text-twins is re-fired LIVE
through the canonical pipeline against the audited probe ledger
(60 rows, 53 rejects / 7 accepts, DET across two probe runs); each of
the 22 precedence-path arms carries an explicit decision-record path
whose FIRES/ANTI alignment is asserted order-invariantly; every scalar is
re-fireable and re-fired; and a final RE-AUDIT re-sources the EMITTED
block into a cleared namespace and re-compares every committed literal
against the ledger -- so emitter drift, chunking drift and quoting drift
all die at mint time, not at read time. The committed clause bytes in
this page are read from the committed witnesses, never re-typed from
plan.

### What the lane-building itself caught (the honest section)

The live replay killed a whole family of would-be-innocent bugs before
one witness byte was trusted. (1) The base's `vapply` is `sapply`: it
attaches value-names to a character result, and the frozen-block
comparisons then failed on an ATTRIBUTE that no printed byte showed --
identical() reddled while both sides looked the same in every dump; the
comparands now strip. (2) The base's `read.csv` is camelCase-gated:
`stringsasfactors`/`colclasses` in the committed idiom died as
"unused argument"; the ledger's first mint carried a phantom sixth
column before the arg casing was fixed -- and the 5-column census was
already on the wall to catch it. (3) The rail needle for the
zero-column-identity pair had been drafted from the plan sketch
(`|4|0|TRUE|FALSE|`) and the measurement put the storage-mode glyph INSIDE
the pair (`|4|0|double|TRUE|FALSE|`); the runner rail and the law
assertion were both corrected against the measured bytes, not the
sketch. (4) `R --slave -f` does not inject `--file=` the way `Rscript`
does (the CLI-face law again): the runner's self-located ROOT silently
fell back to the working directory, the provisioning probe missed
DESCRIPTION, and the `library(msuiter)` fallback loaded a stale
installed build -- whose counts gate was a DIFFERENT face (a
`simpleError` where the tree's face speaks `msuiter_error_catalog`). A
provisioning drift was minutes from being committed as a finding about
the face; the fix is invocation discipline (`Rscript`, sanctioned form),
and the incident is why the provisioning block and its rails ride the
runner verbatim from the CS-16 idiom. (5) The minter's chunker index
math truncated committed clauses (33 committed bytes against a 99-byte
message) while every visible comparison passed -- the emitted-bytes
re-audit now sources the produced file itself and re-verifies every
literal, so a truncation cannot survive the mint. (6) The compiler-tool
probe (a darwin-27 CLT gap, banked law) reddened the local install
path; the C inputs were attested unchanged against the built `.so`
before its timestamp was advanced to restore the skip path -- the
provisioning-trust law honored, not evaded.

### Provenance

The frozen block and the shared code block in both hosts are minted
mechanically from the audited probe ledger (audit green: 60 arms
byte-exact on live re-fire, 8 degen twins, 10/10 fires-and-anti anchors,
10 scalars re-fired); neither is ever hand-edited in place. The plants'
canonical texts hash to the committed dual-kernel checksum
(`plant_sha256=e9e9de78eb43ec9d...`, `spec_sha256=57c4e33e01cea364...`);
reifying the lane reproduces every witness byte for byte. Differentiation
from CS-15 (the reference-container face): CS-15 adjudicated the factory
with its registry-file and cache-path rails; CS-17 adjudicates the
plain in-memory governance container -- its 17-arm validator, the
property-gate boundary MEASURED at three, the digest law shared with the
registry, and the input-class law the snapshot path reaches.

### Gate forensics

The scenarios leg for this lane (the sixteenth) was render-verified
STANDALONE before the full local burn -- the CS-16 lesson applied as
procedure, its columns read off committed bytes only, its adjudication
lines printed TRUE for the record. The T0 seal moved 625 -> 626 with
the generator's refusal witnessed verbatim (the DEFECT line naming 626
against the sealed 625) before the deliberate re-seal, per the budget
law; the reified manifest carries 110 files, the new law file on shard
4, byte-deterministic on re-mint.
